contribution_types.label: UNKNOWN
contribution_types.scope: ECCV 2024 publishes no official contribution-type taxonomy; the Contribution Types mechanism first appears in ECCV 2026.
contribution_types.quote: Papers in the main technical program must describe high-quality, original research.

review_criteria.name: Technical soundness
review_criteria.official_explanation: Accepted papers should be technically sound and contribute to the field.
review_criteria.quote: Each paper that is accepted should be technically sound and make a contribution to the field.

review_criteria.name: Novelty claims must be evidenced
review_criteria.official_explanation: Claims that work has been done before must be supported by specific references.
review_criteria.quote: Be specific about novelty. Claims in a review that the submitted work “has been done before” MUST be backed up with specific references and an explanation of how closely they are related.

review_criteria.name: Novelty and potential impact
review_criteria.official_explanation: Novelty and impact are weighed together with reported performance.
review_criteria.quote: Rather, it is important to weigh both the novelty and potential impact of the work alongside the reported performance.

review_criteria.name: Fit to ECCV subject areas
review_criteria.official_explanation: Out-of-scope papers must be explained and redirected.
review_criteria.quote: If you think the paper is out of scope for ECCV's subject areas, clearly explain why in the review.

review_criteria.name: Reviewer confidentiality and LLM conduct
review_criteria.official_explanation: Allowing an LLM to see a submission is treated as a deliberate breach of referee confidentiality.
review_criteria.quote: It is a significant act of referee misconduct to allow an LLM to see a submission.

mandatory_policy.statement: Papers are limited to 14 pages including figures and tables in the Springer LNCS style, plus reference-only pages.
mandatory_policy.quote: Papers are limited to 14 pages , including figures and tables, in the LNCS style of Springer.

mandatory_policy.statement: Non-anonymized, non-template or over-length papers may be rejected without review.
mandatory_policy.quote: Papers that are not properly anonymized, do not use the template, or have more than 14 pages (excluding references) may be rejected without review.

mandatory_policy.statement: No substantially similar publication may be under submission elsewhere during the ECCV 2024 review period.
mandatory_policy.quote: no publication substantially similar in content has been or will be submitted to another conference, workshop, or journal during the review period.

mandatory_policy.statement: Each author must register institutional conflicts and their DBLP ID in CMT; undeclared or incorrect conflicts may cause summary rejection.
mandatory_policy.quote: each author is required to enter their DBLP ID into their CMT profile

mandatory_policy.statement: Authors are responsible for the entire content of their paper, including misrepresentation, factual inaccuracy or plagiarism.
mandatory_policy.quote: Authors may use any tools they find productive in preparing a paper, but must be aware that they are responsible for the entire content of their paper including any misrepresentation, factual inaccuracy, or plagiarism.

recommended_practice.statement: Code upload as supplementary material is encouraged but not required.
recommended_practice.quote: We encourage (but do not require) authors to upload their code as part of their supplementary material in order to help reviewers assess the quality of the work.

recommended_practice.statement: Authors should avoid introducing new contributions or experimental results in the rebuttal.
recommended_practice.quote: Authors should refrain from including new contributions or experimental results in the rebuttal, especially when not specifically requested to do so by the reviewers.

recommended_practice.statement: Referees may use an LLM to polish review wording only if they never show it the submission and vouch for accuracy.
recommended_practice.quote: Referees may use any device, including a Large Language Model (LLM), to polish their review wording, but must vouch for, and be responsible for, the accuracy of the review.

compliance_checks.requirement: Submission and supplementary material do not identify the authors.
Main paper is at most 14 pages excluding references.
The ECCV 2024 template is used; older templates are not accepted.
All authors have registered institutional conflicts and DBLP IDs in CMT before the registration deadline.
No substantially similar publication is under submission elsewhere during review.

changes_from_prior_year.change: ECCV 2024 uses a new template: the Submission Policies state the template has changed since ECCV 2022 and that older templates must not be used.
ECCV 2024 reviewer guidelines address LLM use in a dedicated FAQ, distinguishing polishing wording from showing a submission to an LLM.

unknown_policies.question: Which ECCV 2024 rules are new relative to ECCV 2022?
unknown_policies.reason: No ECCV 2022 document was retrieved, so the year-over-year delta beyond the explicitly stated template change is not established.

unknown_policies.question: Does ECCV 2024 publish an official contribution-type taxonomy?
unknown_policies.reason: The ECCV 2024 CFP, submission policies and reviewer guidelines retrieved contain no contribution-type taxonomy; ECCV 2026 is the first retrieved edition that publishes one.

unknown_policies.question: Does ECCV 2024 run a separate journal track?
unknown_policies.reason: The retrieved ECCV 2024 documents describe a single main technical program and no journal track; the track is recorded as "main".
